_meta.system: You are an expert music analyst.
_meta._pair_budget_rationale: 12 axes × 1500 directed pairs × ~1.5 s/pair / 12 inflight workers ≈ 38 min wall-clock total on RTX 5090. Bilateral (A→B + B→A) halves discriminative power per directed pair but cancels positional bias → 750 unique pairs per axis covering ~1500 unique tracks (out of 15k). Past round-5: ~10k pairs at 1.48 s median wall-time per pair; each axis's 1500 examples is enough to L2-regularize a 512-d linear probe, with the joint blend leveraging cross-axis information for the final ranking.

axes.label: aggressive
axes.question: Which clip is MORE AGGRESSIVE — harsher, more distorted, more in-your-face, more confrontational? Don't compare for tempo alone; focus on harshness, weight, and energy.
axes.rationale: control axis — should reproduce round-5 BT ranking; baseline check the new corpus + new prompts

axes.label: distorted
axes.question: Which clip has MORE DISTORTION — more clipping, fuzz, saturation, harsh overtones, or driven amp character? Focus on the textural roughness of individual sounds, not how busy or fast the mix is.

axes.label: dense
axes.question: Which clip is MORE DENSE — more simultaneous sounds layered, busier texture, more elements competing for the same frequency space? Don't conflate with loud or distorted; a dense clip can be quiet.
axes.rationale: number of concurrent voices / textural busyness

axes.label: dark
axes.question: Which clip is MORE DARK — more minor-key, lower in pitch, more shadowy / brooding / ominous in mood? Focus on tonal mood and frequency emphasis, not how loud or aggressive.

axes.label: noisy
axes.question: Which clip has MORE NOISE — more inharmonic / atonal layers like white noise, static, hiss, glitches, or non-pitched FX? Distortion of pitched material doesn't count; this is about non-pitched, sound-design layers.
axes.rationale: non-pitched sound layers (vs distortion which is non-linear processing of pitched content)

axes.label: atonal
axes.question: Which clip is MORE ATONAL — less anchored to a clear key or melody, more dissonant or chromatic, harder to hum along to? Focus on pitch organisation, not on whether the sounds themselves are noisy.
axes.rationale: pitched-vs-unpitched / chord ambiguity (Mesh’s existing axis definition)

axes.label: bass-heavy
axes.question: Which clip is MORE BASS-HEAVY — more sub-bass energy, more kick presence, more low-end weight pushing the chest? Focus on the bottom of the spectrum, not on whether the mids are aggressive.

axes.label: fast-feeling
axes.question: Which clip FEELS FASTER — more urgent, more frantic, higher subjective tempo regardless of measured BPM? Focus on the perceived urgency, not the strict beats-per-minute.

axes.label: rhythmically complex
axes.question: Which clip is MORE RHYTHMICALLY COMPLEX — more breakbeat / polyrhythm / syncopation / shifting accents, vs a simpler four-on-the-floor or straight pulse? Focus on rhythmic intricacy, not how fast or loud.

axes.label: vocally intense
axes.question: Which clip has MORE VOCAL INTENSITY — more screaming, growling, shouting, aggressive rapping, harsh vocal effects? A clip with no vocals counts as low. Focus on the vocal performance, not the instrumental.

axes.label: loudness-flat
axes.question: Which clip sounds MORE COMPRESSED / LOUDNESS-FLAT — loud throughout with little dynamic range, vs having quiet-loud-quiet contrast? Focus on the loudness envelope, not on how busy or distorted.

axes.label: harmonically dissonant
axes.question: Which clip has MORE HARMONIC DISSONANCE — more clashing chord intervals, tension chords, tritones, semitone clusters? This is about pitch relationships in the chords, not about noise or atonality.
axes.rationale: chord-level tension (distinct from atonality which is pitched-vs-unpitched)
